case.summary: The transaction of $99.92 made online on 2016-12-01 was flagged by a real-time model with a score of 0.90 and was determined to be fraudulent. The investigation found a shared device profile that had touched five cards in a ±15-day window, linking four other cards with the same email domain and similar amounts, which points to fraud. An analyst was consulted as requested and confirmed the coordinated scheme, supporting the fraud finding. The case was closed as fraud and the card was blocked, the transaction was declined, and the connected cards will be monitored and reported. The exposure was $99.92, which is below the $2,500 threshold for filing a report.

sar.narrative: On December 1, 2016, the cardholder C07987 used card C07987-K2 for an online purchase of $99.92 (transaction 3503878). The transaction was scored 0.90 by the bank’s model, a level that typically indicates a weak input but still triggered review. The device profile used (Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720) had been seen on five different cards within a ±15-day window, a rare pattern, and four other cards (C01104-K2, C01983-K1, C06224-K2, C11309-K1) shared the same email domain and amounts within 10% of $99.92, suggesting coordinated activity. An analyst was consulted after the request for analyst information and confirmed that the shared device profile links the four other cards in a coordinated scheme. Based on policy R6, the shared origin and the exposure of $99.92 (≤ $2,500) warranted filing a report and monitoring the connected cards. The case was closed as fraud, the card was blocked, and the transaction was declined. The linked cards involved are C07987-K2, C01104-K2, C01983-K1, C06224-K2, and C11309-K1.
